application_fee.details: The fee can be paid by credit card, debit card or net banking through the online payment gateway on the portal, right after registration. When paying by card or net banking, the payment is valid only after the bank confirms it. Keep the fee receipt safe after payment. A candidate who does not complete the application by the last date after One Time Registration and payment will not have the application accepted. Once the fee is paid, it will not be refunded in any situation and it will not be adjusted against another application.

age_limit.details: Applications without a date of birth, or from candidates who are over 62 years of age on 1 July 2026, will not be accepted. Only the date of birth recorded in the High School or equivalent certificate is valid. No other document is accepted as proof of date of birth. The notification does not give any age relaxation for any category.

how_to_apply: The notification gives the following application process. Only online applications through the Commission's OTR-based system are accepted. Applications sent by any other means will not be accepted.
Visit the official website www.upessc.up.gov.in.
Complete One Time Registration (OTR). Registration is compulsory before applying.
Read the User Manual (Hindi and English) and watch the tutorial videos available on the website before applying.
Fill the registration and application form in English only.
Upload your scanned signature on a white background and a passport-size photograph, both in JPG or JPEG format with a file size between 10 KB and 100 KB.
Upload certificates and documents in PDF format, with a file size between 20 KB and 200 KB.
Pay the application fee online as per your post (₹2,000 for Principal, ₹1,500 for Headmaster).
Submit the application. Take three printouts for future use and keep the fee receipt safe.
The notification does not give a direct application link or screen-by-screen steps. Candidates should use the official website and the User Manual.
After the application is finally submitted, no change is allowed in category, sub-category, date of birth, gender and similar details. Fill in all details correctly while registering and submitting.
A chance to correct errors will be given until the date fixed by the Commission (25 November 2026). Fees paid for an erroneous application will not be refunded.
If a candidate submits more than one application for the same post, only the last application is accepted and all others are treated as cancelled.
An application will be rejected if the photograph or signature is not uploaded in the prescribed size, or if the declaration is not accepted.

If the declaration made in the application is found to be false, the candidate's candidature will be cancelled. The candidate may be debarred from this and all other selections/examinations and face other penal action.

If at any stage it comes to light that a candidate has hidden information or filled it wrongly, the candidature will be cancelled and the candidate may be debarred from future examinations/selections.
Candidates must keep three copies of the submitted application. Two copies must be submitted to the Commission office at the time of interview, with two separate sets of the documents.
A candidate who tries to cheat, shows indiscipline or misbehaves in the exam hall can have candidature cancelled and may be barred from future examinations.

Bring a black ball point pen to the exam hall. Use only black ball point pen to fill the boxes and bubbles on the OMR sheet. Blue or other colour ball pens, fountain pens, gel pens, sketch pens, H.B. pencils and whitener are prohibited.
Once a bubble is darkened, no change is accepted. If more than one bubble is darkened for a question, it will not be evaluated and no marks are given.
Use of eraser, nail, blade or whitener on the OMR sheet is prohibited. An OMR sheet damaged in any way will be cancelled and not evaluated.

Fill the required information on the OMR sheet correctly and darken only the related bubbles. Do not make any other mark such as dots or ink marks. If the OMR sheet is not evaluated because of a mistake, the candidate is solely responsible.
Candidates can download the OMR answer sheet format from the Commission's website and practise before the exam.

Candidates with disabilities will be given a scribe as per the Government Orders dated 4 December 2019 and 8 September 2022. The scribe must be brought by the candidate. Such candidates must get the written exam scribe details registered at the Commission office at least one week before the exam. An additional 20 minutes per hour is allowed. No travel allowance is paid to the scribe.

content_sections.heading: UPESSC Principal Headmaster Vacancy 2026
content_sections.text: UPESSC has invited online applications for 1,475 Principal posts and 1,172 Headmaster posts in aided non-government schools. The notification states that the number of vacancies may increase or decrease. The notification states that the requisition list includes posts relating to Special Appeal No. 376/2026 (Rajkumar Singh and others versus State of U.P. and others), in compliance with the order of the Hon'ble High Court dated 15 April 2026. These posts are already counted within the totals above. The notification refers to the requisition list for these posts as Appendix-4 in this clause. The contents page of each PDF lists the school-wise requisition as Table-2 (Sarani-2). It runs from page 15 to page 62 in the Principal notification and from page 15 to page 54 in the Headmaster notification. It gives the division, district, school name, requisition year, boys/girls category, type of institution and the number of posts for each school. All vacancies are unreserved. The Directorate of Secondary Education, Prayagraj has informed the Commission that the Principal and Headmaster posts are identified for candidates with benchmark disabilities in these sub-categories: O.A., O.L., B., B.A., L.V., D., H.H., L.C., D.W., A.A.V., A.S.D., S.L.D., I.D., M.I., B.L., B.L.A., B.H. and M.D.Y. The notification defines physical disability as covering: (a) blindness and low vision; (b) deaf and hard of hearing; (c) locomotor disability, including cerebral palsy, cured leprosy, dwarfism, acid attack victims and muscular dystrophy; (d) autism, intellectual disability, specific learning disability and mental illness; and (e) multiple disabilities from among (a) to (d), including deaf-blindness. Note 2 of the notification quotes the Government Order dated 18 April 2022 (point 5): a person with a disability can be appointed against an unreserved vacancy provided the post is identified as suitable for that person's category of disability.

content_sections.heading: UPESSC Principal Headmaster Appointment and School Allotment
content_sections.text: Allotment of schools to selected candidates is done by the authorised officer, the Director, Secondary Education, U.P., Prayagraj. The Commission will conduct the written exam and interview for the Principal and Headmaster posts in aided non-government schools (boys/girls). Appearing in the written exam or even succeeding in it does not make a candidate finally eligible for selection as Principal or Headmaster. Candidates must confirm for themselves that they meet the minimum qualifications. The Commission will provisionally allow candidates into the written exam on the basis of the information given, but if it is found later that the candidate is not eligible or the application should not have been accepted at the initial stage, the candidature will be cancelled. If a recommendation has already been made for appointment, it will be withdrawn. In a dispute, the candidate must first make a representation to the Commission.
